heroHeadline: Bloomberg: US-Iran Agree to 60-Day Truce Pending Trump Sign-Off; Pakistan FM Dar Meets Rubio; Lebanon-Israel Pentagon Military Talks; IRGC Sanctions — Day 91
heroSubtitle: Day 91 (May 29, 2026): Bloomberg reported that the United States and Iran agreed to a 60-day truce extension framework pending President Trump's formal sign-off — the first time a major wire service described the sides as having 'agreed' on a framework rather than 'progressing toward' one. Trump met with his NSC team and posted on Truth Social signaling near-acceptance of the deal's key terms: Hormuz reopens with no tolls, Iran clears mines, US issues sanctions waivers for Iranian oil, Iran commits to no nuclear weapon, and a 60-day window opens for HEU disposal talks. Iranian FM Baghaei tempered expectations, saying progress had been made on 'many issues' but 'no imminent agreement should be expected.' Pakistan FM Ishaq Dar flew to Washington for talks with Secretary Rubio — reinforcing Pakistan's central mediation role ahead of the anticipated announcement. The US Treasury simultaneously imposed new sanctions on IRGC oil financing networks, including Hong Kong-based entities. At the Pentagon, Lebanese, Israeli, and American military delegations met for the first dedicated security track session on Israeli withdrawal, Lebanese Army deployment, and Hezbollah disarmament. The June 2–3 Doha fourth round remains the formal diplomatic gate for any MoU signature. Brent crude fell 1.2% to ~$92.56/bbl — May 2026's worst month since COVID, down ~19% from April highs.
